messages.subject: Lavaan simulateData standardized=TRUE
parts:
Hi all,

Newbie here, so apologies if I don't understand the group etiquette! 

Has anyone tried to simulate data using standardized loadings in the model statement and specifying standardized = TRUE?  

I am getting different results when I read in standardized and unstandardized loadings.  

When I create the model statement for the standardized model, I only include the standardized loadings and factor correlations, and then add standardized=TRUE.

When I create the model statement for the unstandardized model, I include the unstandardized loadings, factor correlations, and the unstandardized residual error variances (and leave out standardized=TRUE since the default is FALSE).

Also, can simulateData handle correlated residuals when standardized=TRUE?  I've tried entering the correlation and the covariance, and both times I get the error: "please provide better fixed values for (co)variances".  There is no issue when I'm using the unstandardized model.

Am I using standardized=TRUE incorrectly?

For what it's worth, using the simstandard package seems to resolve most issues with reading in standardized loadings (although the lavaan errors may very well be my own user error!).

Thank you!!!

Melissa

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan simulateData standardized=TRUE
parts:
The error sounds like you are providing population parameters that imply correlations > 1 (or variances that exceed 1).  Setting standardized=TRUE does not transform any of your specified covariance-structure parameters.  It merely tells lavaan to automatically choose residual variances that would lead to total variances == 1, so that you don't have to specify them in your population model syntax.  If you know your standardized population values already, you are better off just using those.
